what_its_for: This combination birth control pill helps prevent pregnancy. It may also be used to treat moderate acne in women who choose to use birth control pills, and to help with the emotional and physical symptoms of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). It contains two hormones — drospirenone (a progestin) and ethinyl estradiol (an estrogen) — that work together to stop ovulation, thicken cervical mucus, and change the lining of the uterus to help prevent pregnancy.
how_to_take: Take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day. Try to pick a time that is easy to remember, like brushing your teeth in the morning or at bedtime. Swallow the pill whole with or without food. If the pill upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or at bedtime. Follow the order of pills in your pack — do not skip pills or take them out of order. Some packs contain reminder (inactive) pills for the last days of the cycle — take these too to keep your daily habit.
dosing: Take one active pill every day for 21 or 24 days (depending on your pack), followed by inactive reminder pills for the remaining days. Most packs are 28 days total. Start your first pack either on the first day of your period or on the first Sunday after your period begins, depending on your doctor's instructions. Use a backup method of birth control (like condoms) for the first 7 days if you are not starting on the first day of your period.
missed_dose: If you miss 1 pill: Take it as soon as you remember, even if it means taking 2 pills in one day. Then continue taking one pill per day as usual. You likely do not need backup contraception. If you miss 2 pills in a row in Week 1 or Week 2: Take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day. Then take one pill per day for the rest of the pack. Use a backup method of birth control for 7 days. If you miss 2 pills in a row in Week 3, or miss 3 or more pills in a row: Throw out the rest of the pack and start a new pack the same day (Sunday starters should keep taking pills until Sunday, then start a new pack). Use backup contraception for 7 days. You may not have a period that month — this is expected. If you miss a period after missing pills, contact your doctor or take a pregnancy test. If you miss any reminder (inactive) pills, simply throw them away and continue with the pack.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use pills past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking cigarettes while taking this medication, especially if you are over 35 years old. Smoking combined with birth control pills significantly increases the risk of serious blood clots, heart attack, and stroke. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice in large amounts, as it may affect how the medication works. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medications you take, because some drugs can make your birth control less effective or cause dangerous interactions — including certain antibiotics (like rifampin), antifungals, seizure medications, and herbal supplements like St. John's Wort. Avoid prolonged periods of sitting still (like long flights), as this medication can increase the risk of blood clots — try to move around when possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to an emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain or tightness, shortness of breath, coughing up blood (possible signs of a blood clot in the lungs); severe abdominal or stomach pain; sudden severe headache, vision changes, slurred speech, weakness or numbness in an arm or leg (possible signs of stroke); leg pain, swelling, or warmth (possible signs of a blood clot); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); breast lumps; signs of depression or mood changes; unusually heavy or irregular vaginal bleeding; two missed periods in a row or signs of pregnancy. Also contact your doctor if you miss two periods in a row, if you have severe nausea or vomiting, if you notice a significant increase in blood pressure, or if any new or worsening symptoms concern you.
when_it_works: This birth control pill begins to prevent pregnancy right away if you start it on the first day of your period. If you start on any other day, it takes about 7 days to become fully effective, so use a backup method of contraception (such as condoms) during that time. For treating acne or PMDD, it may take several weeks to a few months before you notice an improvement. Be patient and continue taking the pill as directed.
special_populations: Women over 35 who smoke should NOT use this medication due to a high risk of serious heart problems, blood clots, and stroke. This medication is not appropriate for use after menopause. It should not be used during pregnancy — stop taking it immediately if you become pregnant and talk to your doctor. Drospirenone may increase potassium levels in the blood, so it should be used with caution by women with kidney, liver, or adrenal gland problems, or those taking medications that also raise potassium (such as certain blood pressure medications, potassium supplements, or anti-inflammatory drugs). Women who are breastfeeding should talk to their doctor before using this pill, as estrogen-containing pills may reduce milk supply. Teenagers who have not yet had their first period should not use this medication.
